newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Philippines and the United Kingdom sign seven private sector agreements which are expected to expand their economic ties. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- President Ramos has issued an order declaring a moratorium on new duty-free stores in Subic and Clark until a control system is established by the Bureau of Customs. (MALAYA)
- The military has accused a Moslem rebel group holding peace talks with the government of being involved in a rash of kidnappings in Central Mindanao. (INQUIRER)
- The International Monetary Fund supports the Philippine government's move to extend the country's three-year economic programme with the Fund. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission ordered its examiners yesterday to conduct another investigation and submit another report on charges of price manipulation involving the four biggest foreign-owned brokerage firms at the Philippine Stock Exchange. (STAR/TIMES)

- Growth of domestic credit continued to slow down in April to 34.7 percent from 37.4 percent a month ago, dispelling fears the economy is about to overheat, the Central Bank reported. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
